query_text: I just finished reading the Expanse novels. Wow. Any recommendations for a new book?

parts.text:
Finishing *The Expanse* is a monumental reading milestone, but the "book hangover" it leaves behind is very real. Because the series does so many things well—from gritty, realistic physics and found-family crew dynamics to Solar System politics and mind-bending alien mysteries—the best recommendation depends on which of those elements you loved the most. 

Here is a curated roadmap of where to go next:

### 1. If you just want more from the authors of *The Expanse*
Before leaving Daniel Abraham and Ty Franck (writing as James S.A. Corey) behind, check out:
*   **The Expanse Short Stories:** If you only read the nine main novels, grab ***Memory's Legion***. It is a compilation of all the *Expanse* novellas and short stories. It features vital backstories (like Amos's life on Earth in *The Churn*) and the ultimate epilogue to the entire series (*The Sins of Our Fathers*).
*   **The Captive's War Series (Starts with *The Mercy of Gods*):** This is the authors' brand-new sci-fi trilogy. It follows a colony of human scientists who are captured by a massive, ancient alien empire called the Carryx. To survive, the humans must prove their utility in an endless galactic war. It has the same brilliant character-driven pacing and survival instincts as *The Expanse*, but on a much more bizarre, grand alien scale. *(Bonus: Book 2, **The Faith of Beasts**, was recently released in April 2026, so you won't have to wait to keep reading!)*

### 2. If you loved the *Rocinante* crew & gritty space travel
*   ***Shards of Earth* (The Final Architecture Series) by Adrian Tchaikovsky**
    *   **The Vibe:** *The Expanse* meets *Mass Effect*. 
    *   **Why you'll love it:** It follows a ragtag, found-family crew on a salvage spaceship trying to scrape by. Decades prior, Earth was literally reshaped into a hollowed-out sculpture by terrifying, moon-sized entities called "Architects" who suddenly vanished. Now, the crew discovers signs that the Architects might be coming back. It’s got great action, incredibly deep lore, and excellent political tension.
*   ***Revelation Space* by Alastair Reynolds**
    *   **The Vibe:** Gothic, noir-ish, ultra-hard sci-fi.
    *   **Why you'll love it:** Written by a former European Space Agency astrophysicist, this book treats space with terrifying realism. There is no faster-than-light travel, meaning journeys take years, crews suffer from time dilation, and ancient secrets are buried deep. It has a gritty, "used-universe" aesthetic that will feel instantly familiar to fans of the Belt.

### 3. If you loved the mind-bending alien mysteries & cosmic dread
*   ***The Three-Body Problem* (Remembrance of Earth's Past Trilogy) by Cixin Liu**
    *   **The Vibe:** High-concept hard sci-fi, first contact, and existential dread.
    *   **Why you'll love it:** If the protomolecule and the "Ring Builders" mystery were your favorite parts of *The Expanse*, this is the logical next step. It begins during China's Cultural Revolution when a secret military project sends signals into space, which are intercepted by an alien civilization on the brink of destruction. It is a slow burn that escalates into some of the most mind-bending, epic-scale sci-fi ever written.
*   ***Children of Time* by Adrian Tchaikovsky**
    *   **The Vibe:** Evolutionary epic, dying Earth, and grand scale.
    *   **Why you'll love it:** Recommended highly by the authors of *The Expanse* themselves. It tells two parallel stories: a generation ship carrying the last remnants of humanity looking for a home, and the rapid, forced evolution of a species of spiders on a terraformed planet. It is an incredibly smart, compassionate, and masterfully paced epic.

### 4. If you loved the Solar System politics & high-stakes action
*   ***Red Rising* by Pierce Brown**
    *   **The Vibe:** *The Hunger Games* meets *Gladiator* in space.
    *   **Why you'll love it:** Set in a color-coded caste system across a fully colonized Solar System, it follows Darrow, a low-caste "Red" mining the interior of Mars, who infiltrates the ruling "Gold" class to bring down the society from the inside. It is much more stylized and operatic than *The Expanse*, but if you loved the Martian militarism, the political backstabbing of Avasarala, and non-stop, adrenaline-fueled action, this series is addictive.

**Where to start?** If you want to jump straight into something with a very similar writing style, go with ***The Mercy of Gods***. If you want a brand-new space opera with a great crew dynamic, start with ***Shards of Earth***.
